passages.text: In the third year of the reign of Hoshea son of Elah over Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the son of Ahaz.
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Hoshea was the son of Elah.
Hoshea was king of Israel.
In the third year of Hoshea’s reign over Israel, Hezekiah became king of Judah.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁלֹ֔שׁ לְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בֶּן־ אֵלָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ חִזְקִיָּ֥ה בֶן־ אָחָ֖ז מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah became king of Judah when he was twenty-five years old.
He ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years.
His mother was Abi.
Abi was the daughter of Zechariah.
passages.original: בֶּן־ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָתֵ֙שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ אֲבִ֖י בַּת־ זְכַרְיָֽה׃

passages.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father David had done.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah did what was right.
The LORD saw that Hezekiah did what was right.
Hezekiah acted as David had acted.
David was Hezekiah’s ancestor.
David also did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: He removed the high places, shattered the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles. He also demolished the bronze snake called Nehushtan that Moses had made, for up to that time the Israelites had burned incense to it.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah removed the high places.
Hezekiah shattered the sacred pillars.
Hezekiah cut down the Asherah poles.
Hezekiah demolished the bronze snake that Moses had made.
The Israelites had burned incense to the bronze snake until that time.
Hezekiah called the bronze snake Nehushtan.
passages.original: ה֣וּא׀ הֵסִ֣יר אֶת־ הַבָּמ֗וֹת וְשִׁבַּר֙ אֶת־ הַמַּצֵּבֹ֔ת וְכָרַ֖ת אֶת־ הָֽאֲשֵׁרָ֑ה וְכִתַּת֩ נְחַ֨שׁ הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֗ה כִּ֣י עַד־ הַיָּמִ֤ים הָהֵ֙מָּה֙ הָי֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מְקַטְּרִ֣ים ל֔וֹ וַיִּקְרָא־ ל֖וֹ נְחֻשְׁתָּֽן׃

passages.text: Hezekiah trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. No king of Judah was like him, either before him or after him.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah trusted in the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
No king of Judah was like Hezekiah.
No king before Hezekiah was like him.
No king after Hezekiah was like him.
passages.original: בַּיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּטָ֑ח וְאַחֲרָ֞יו לֹא־ הָיָ֣ה כָמֹ֗הוּ בְּכֹל֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: He remained faithful to the LORD and did not turn from following Him; he kept the commandments that the LORD had given Moses.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah stayed close to the LORD.
Hezekiah did not turn away from the LORD.
Hezekiah obeyed the LORD’s commands.
The LORD had given these commands to Moses.
passages.original: וַיִּדְבַּק֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה לֹא־ סָ֖ר מֵאַֽחֲרָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁמֹר֙ מִצְוֺתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃

passages.text: And the LORD was with Hezekiah, and he prospered wherever he went. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
The LORD was with Hezekiah.
Hezekiah succeeded in everything he did.
Hezekiah rebelled against the king of Assyria.
Hezekiah did not serve the king of Assyria.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ יֵצֵ֖א יַשְׂכִּ֑יל וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד בְּמֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֖וּר וְלֹ֥א עֲבָדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders, from watchtower to fortified city.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah fought against the Philistines.
Hezekiah defeated the Philistines.
Hezekiah drove them back as far as Gaza.
Hezekiah took control of Gaza’s borders.
Hezekiah defeated the Philistines from the watchtower.
Hezekiah defeated them up to the fortified city.
passages.original: הֽוּא־ הִכָּ֧ה אֶת־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֛ים עַד־ עַזָּ֖ה וְאֶת־ גְּבוּלֶ֑יהָ מִמִּגְדַּ֥ל נוֹצְרִ֖ים עַד־ עִ֥יר מִבְצָֽר׃פ

passages.text: In the fourth year of Hezekiah’s reign, which was the seventh year of the reign of Hoshea son of Elah over Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against Samaria and besieged it.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hoshea son of Elah was king of Israel.
Hezekiah had reigned for four years.
Hoshea had reigned for seven years.
Shalmaneser was king of Assyria.
Shalmaneser marched against Samaria.
Samaria was the capital of Israel.
Shalmaneser besieged Samaria.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הָֽרְבִיעִית֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ הִ֚יא הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ית לְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בֶּן־ אֵלָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עָלָ֞ה שַׁלְמַנְאֶ֧סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֛וּר עַל־ שֹׁמְר֖וֹן וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: And at the end of three years, the Assyrians captured it. So Samaria was captured in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Assyrians attacked Samaria.
They laid siege to the city for three years.
At the end of three years, the Assyrians captured Samaria.
This happened in the sixth year of King Hezekiah of Judah.
This was also the ninth year of King Hoshea of Israel.
Samaria fell to the Assyrians at that time.
passages.original: וַֽיִּלְכְּדֻ֗הָ מִקְצֵה֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים בִּשְׁנַת־ שֵׁ֖שׁ לְחִזְקִיָּ֑ה הִ֣יא שְׁנַת־ תֵּ֗שַׁע לְהוֹשֵׁ֙עַ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נִלְכְּדָ֖ה שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: The king of Assyria exiled the Israelites to Assyria and settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria took the Israelites away from their land.
He sent the Israelites into exile in Assyria.
He settled the Israelites in Halah.
He settled them in Gozan, by the Habor River.
He also settled them in the cities of the Medes.
passages.original: וַיֶּ֧גֶל מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַשּׁ֑וּרָה וַיַּנְחֵ֞ם בַּחְלַ֧ח וּבְחָב֛וֹר נְהַ֥ר גּוֹזָ֖ן וְעָרֵ֥י מָדָֽי׃

passages.text: This happened because they did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God, but violated His covenant—all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded—and would neither listen nor obey.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God.
They broke His covenant.
Moses was the servant of the LORD.
Moses commanded them in everything God told him.
The Israelites did not listen to Moses.
The Israelites did not obey God’s commands.
This is why these things happened to them.
passages.original: עַ֣ל׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ שָׁמְע֗וּ בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּעַבְרוּ֙ אֶת־ בְּרִית֔וֹ אֵ֚ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה עֶ֣בֶד יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א עָשֽׂוּ׃פ

passages.text: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah had ruled for fourteen years.
Sennacherib was king of Assyria.
Sennacherib attacked Judah.
He attacked all the fortified cities in Judah.
Sennacherib captured all those cities.
passages.original: וּבְאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֗ה עָלָ֞ה סַנְחֵרִ֤יב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁוּר֙ עַ֣ל כָּל־ עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה הַבְּצֻר֖וֹת וַֽיִּתְפְּשֵֽׂם׃

passages.text: So Hezekiah king of Judah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have done wrong; withdraw from me, and I will pay whatever you demand from me.” And the king of Assyria exacted from Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah sent a message to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria was at Lachish.
Hezekiah said, “I have done wrong.”
Hezekiah asked the king of Assyria to withdraw from him.
Hezekiah said he would pay whatever the king of Assyria demanded.
The king of Assyria set a price for Hezekiah.
He demanded three hundred talents of silver.
He also demanded thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah agreed to pay this amount.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח חִזְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֣ה אֶל־ מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁוּר֩׀ לָכִ֨ישָׁה׀ לֵאמֹ֤ר׀ חָטָ֙אתִי֙ שׁ֣וּב מֵֽעָלַ֔י אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ תִּתֵּ֥ן עָלַ֖י אֶשָּׂ֑א וַיָּ֨שֶׂם מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֜וּר עַל־ חִזְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֗ה שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ כִּכַּר־ כֶּ֔סֶף וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים כִּכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב׃

passages.text: Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Sennacherib was the king of Assyria.
Hezekiah gave Sennacherib all the silver he could find.
He took silver from the house of the LORD.
He also took silver from the treasuries of the royal palace.
Hezekiah gave all this silver to the king of Assyria.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּן֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔ה אֶת־ כָּל־ הַכֶּ֖סֶף הַנִּמְצָ֣א בֵית־ יְהוָ֑ה וּבְאֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: At that time Hezekiah stripped the gold with which he had plated the doors and doorposts of the temple of the LORD, and he gave it to the king of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
At that time, Hezekiah removed the gold from the doors of the temple of the LORD.
Hezekiah also removed the gold from the doorposts of the temple.
Hezekiah himself had put this gold on the doors and doorposts.
Hezekiah gave this gold to the king of Assyria.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא קִצַּ֨ץ חִזְקִיָּ֜ה אֶת־ דַּלְת֨וֹת הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וְאֶת־ הָאֹ֣מְנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִפָּ֔ה חִזְקִיָּ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃פ

passages.text: Nevertheless, the king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rabsaris, and the Rabshakeh, along with a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. They advanced up to Jerusalem and stationed themselves by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria sent three officials from Lachish.
He sent the Tartan.
He sent the Rabsaris.
He sent the Rabshakeh.
He sent them to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem.
He sent them with a large army.
They marched toward Jerusalem.
They arrived at Jerusalem.
They stood by the aqueduct of the upper pool.
This aqueduct is on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֡וּר אֶת־ תַּרְתָּ֥ן וְאֶת־ רַב־ סָרִ֣יס׀ וְאֶת־ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֨ה מִן־ לָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּחֵ֥יל כָּבֵ֖ד יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיַּעֲל֣וּ וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ בִּתְעָלַת֙ הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הָֽעֶלְיוֹנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֕ר בִּמְסִלַּ֖ת שְׂדֵ֥ה כוֹבֵֽס׃

passages.text: Then they called for the king; and Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebnah the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to them.
passages.sermon:
The Assyrian officials called for King Hezekiah.
Eliakim went out to meet them.
Eliakim was the son of Hilkiah.
Eliakim was in charge of the palace.
Shebnah also went out to them.
Shebnah was the scribe.
Joah also went out to them.
Joah was the son of Asaph.
Joah was the recorder.
passages.original: וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֵּצֵ֧א אֲלֵהֶ֛ם אֶלְיָקִ֥ים בֶּן־ חִלְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ הַבָּ֑יִת וְשֶׁבְנָה֙ הַסֹּפֵ֔ר וְיוֹאָ֥ח בֶּן־ אָסָ֖ף הַמַּזְכִּֽיר׃

passages.text: The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah that this is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours?
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was a high official from Assyria.
He spoke to the men who came out from Jerusalem.
He gave them a message for King Hezekiah of Judah.
He said, “This is what the great king says.
The great king is the king of Assyria.
He asks you a question.
He says, ‘What is the reason for your confidence?
Why do you trust so much?’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֔ה אִמְרוּ־ נָ֖א אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר מָ֧ה הַבִּטָּח֛וֹן הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּטָֽחְתָּ׃

passages.text: You claim to have a strategy and strength for war, but these are empty words. In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh spoke to the officials from Judah.
He represented the king of Assyria.
He addressed Hezekiah’s representatives.
He said, “You say you have advice and strength for war.
But these are only words.
You do not have real power.
You do not have real plans.
You have rebelled against me, the king of Assyria.
Who are you trusting now?”
passages.original: אָמַ֙רְתָּ֙ אַךְ־ דְּבַר־ שְׂפָתַ֔יִם עֵצָ֥ה וּגְבוּרָ֖ה לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ עַל־ מִ֣י בָטַ֔חְתָּ כִּ֥י מָרַ֖דְתָּ בִּֽי׃

passages.text: Look now, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh spoke to Hezekiah’s messengers.
He was an official of the king of Assyria.
He said, “You are trusting in Egypt.”
Egypt is like a broken reed.
A broken reed cannot support anyone.
If a person leans on it, it will pierce his hand.
Pharaoh is the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh is like this broken reed to everyone who trusts in him.
passages.original: עַתָּ֡ה הִנֵּ֣ה בָטַ֣חְתָּ לְּךָ֡ עַל־ מִשְׁעֶנֶת֩ הַקָּנֶ֨ה הָרָצ֤וּץ הַזֶּה֙ עַל־ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִסָּמֵ֥ךְ אִישׁ֙ עָלָ֔יו וּבָ֥א בְכַפּ֖וֹ וּנְקָבָ֑הּ כֵּ֚ן פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֔יִם לְכָֽל־ הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem: ‘You must worship before this altar in Jerusalem’?
passages.sermon:
You may say to me, “We trust in the LORD our God.”
Hezekiah is the king of Judah.
Hezekiah removed the high places and altars of the LORD in Judah and Jerusalem.
Hezekiah commanded Judah and Jerusalem to worship only at the altar in Jerusalem.
You claim to trust in the LORD, even though Hezekiah removed His high places and altars.
Hezekiah told the people, “You must worship before this altar in Jerusalem.”
passages.original: וְכִי־ תֹאמְר֣וּן אֵלַ֔י אֶל־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ בָּטָ֑חְנוּ הֲלוֹא־ ה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵסִ֤יר חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶת־ בָּמֹתָ֣יו וְאֶת־ מִזְבְּחֹתָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִפְנֵי֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ הַזֶּ֔ה תִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh spoke to the leaders of Judah.
He represented the king of Assyria.
He challenged them to make an agreement with his master, the king of Assyria.
He said, "I will give you two thousand horses."
He added, "This is only if you are able to provide riders for them."
He implied that Judah did not have enough trained men to ride the horses.
He showed that Judah was weak compared to Assyria.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ הִתְעָ֣רֶב נָ֔א אֶת־ אֲדֹנִ֖י אֶת־ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לְךָ֙ אַלְפַּ֣יִם סוּסִ֔ים אִם־ תּוּכַ֕ל לָ֥תֶת לְךָ֖ רֹכְבִ֥ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For how can you repel a single officer among the least of my master’s servants when you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh is the spokesman for the king of Assyria.
He speaks to the leaders of Judah.
He challenges their ability to resist Assyria.
He says, "You trust in Egypt for help."
"You hope Egypt will give you chariots and horsemen."
"But you cannot defeat even one of my master's lowest officers."
"You cannot stand against even the least of Assyria's servants."
"You have no real strength against us."
"You depend on Egypt, but it will not save you."
passages.original: וְאֵ֣יךְ תָּשִׁ֗יב אֵ֠ת פְּנֵ֨י פַחַ֥ת אַחַ֛ד עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י הַקְּטַנִּ֑ים וַתִּבְטַ֤ח לְךָ֙ עַל־ מִצְרַ֔יִם לְרֶ֖כֶב וּלְפָרָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: So now, was it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this place to destroy it? The LORD Himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was the chief spokesman for the king of Assyria.
He spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
He said, “I did not come here without the LORD’s command.
The LORD told me to come up against this land.
The LORD said to destroy it.
I am here because the LORD Himself sent me.”
passages.original: עַתָּה֙ הֲמִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עָלִ֛יתִי עַל־ הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לְהַשְׁחִת֑וֹ יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י עֲלֵ֛ה עַל־ הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְהַשְׁחִיתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, along with Shebnah and Joah, said to the Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Do not speak with us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.”
passages.sermon:
Eliakim was the son of Hilkiah.
Shebnah and Joah were with him.
They spoke to the Rabshakeh.
They said, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic.
We understand Aramaic.
Do not speak with us in Hebrew.
The people on the wall can hear Hebrew.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן־ חִ֠לְקִיָּהוּ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨ה וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל־ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֗ה דַּבֶּר־ נָ֤א אֶל־ עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲרָמִ֔ית כִּ֥י שֹׁמְעִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְאַל־ תְּדַבֵּ֤ר עִמָּ֙נוּ֙ יְהוּדִ֔ית בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ הַחֹמָֽה׃

passages.text: But the Rabshakeh replied, “Has my master sent me to speak these words only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are destined with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was the chief officer of the king of Assyria.
The Rabshakeh spoke to Eliakim, Shebnah, and Joah.
He answered their request.
He said, “My master did not send me only to your master and to you.
He sent me also to the men sitting on the wall.
These men will suffer with you.
They will eat their own dung.
They will drink their own urine with you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם רַב־ שָׁקֵ֗ה הַעַ֨ל אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ וְאֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲדֹנִ֔י לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲלֹ֣א עַל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ עַל־ הַ֣חֹמָ֔ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת חֲרֵיהֶם וְלִשְׁתּ֛וֹת אֶת־ שֵׁינֵיהֶם עִמָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebrew: “Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
passages.sermon:
The Rabshakeh was an official from Assyria.
He stood up.
He called out in a loud voice.
He spoke in Hebrew.
He said, “Listen to the word of the great king.
The great king is the king of Assyria.”
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב־ שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל־ גָּד֖וֹל יְהוּדִ֑ית וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר וַיֹּ֔אמֶר שִׁמְע֛וּ דְּבַר־ הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הַגָּד֖וֹל מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you; he cannot deliver you from my hand.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
He said, “Do not let Hezekiah deceive you.
Hezekiah cannot save you from my power.
He cannot rescue you from my hand.”
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אַל־ יַשִּׁ֥יא לָכֶ֖ם חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּי־ לֹ֣א יוּכַ֔ל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD when he says, ‘The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah is the king of Judah.
The king of Assyria sent a message to the people of Jerusalem.
He said, “Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD.”
Hezekiah says, ‘The LORD will surely save us.’
Hezekiah says, ‘This city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.’
Do not believe Hezekiah when he says this.
passages.original: וְאַל־ יַבְטַ֨ח אֶתְכֶ֤ם חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר הַצֵּ֥ל יַצִּילֵ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ אֶת־ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink water from his own cistern, until I come and take you away to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey—so that you may live and not die. But do not listen to Hezekiah, for he misleads you when he says, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He says, "Do not listen to Hezekiah."
Hezekiah is your king.
Hezekiah tells you to trust in the LORD.
But I, the king of Assyria, say this to you.
Make peace with me.
Come out to me.
If you do this, each of you will eat from his own vine.
Each of you will eat from his own fig tree.
Each of you will drink water from his own cistern.
You will have these things until I come.
Then I will take you away to another land.
This land will be like your own land.
It will be a land of grain and new wine.
It will be a land of bread and vineyards.
It will be a land of olive trees and honey.
You will live there.
You will not die.
Do not listen to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah misleads you when he says, 'The LORD will deliver us.'
passages.original: אַֽל־ תִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר עֲשֽׂוּ־ אִתִּ֤י בְרָכָה֙ וּצְא֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְאִכְל֤וּ אִישׁ־ גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּאֵֽנָת֔וֹ וּשְׁת֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מֵֽי־ בוֹרֽוֹ׃ עַד־ בֹּאִי֩ וְלָקַחְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֜ם אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּאַרְצְכֶ֗ם אֶרֶץ֩ דָּגָ֨ן וְתִיר֜וֹשׁ אֶ֧רֶץ לֶ֣חֶם וּכְרָמִ֗ים אֶ֣רֶץ זֵ֤ית יִצְהָר֙ וּדְבַ֔שׁ וִֽחְי֖וּ וְלֹ֣א תָמֻ֑תוּ וְאַֽל־ תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּֽי־ יַסִּ֤ית אֶתְכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֖ה יַצִּילֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria is speaking.
He asks a question about the gods of other nations.
He says, "Has any nation's god saved its land from my hand?"
He means, "Has any god delivered his people from the king of Assyria?"
passages.original: הַהַצֵּ֥ל הִצִּ֛ילוּ אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ אַרְצ֑וֹ מִיַּ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
He asked about the gods of Hamath and Arpad.
He said, “Where are the gods of Hamath?”
He said, “Where are the gods of Arpad?”
He asked about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah.
He said, “Where are the gods of Sepharvaim?”
He said, “Where are the gods of Hena?”
He said, “Where are the gods of Ivvah?”
He asked if these gods saved Samaria from his power.
He said, “Did these gods deliver Samaria from my hand?”
passages.original: אַיֵּה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י חֲמָ֜ת וְאַרְפָּ֗ד אַיֵּ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י סְפַרְוַ֖יִם הֵנַ֣ע וְעִוָּ֑ה כִּֽי־ הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־ שֹׁמְר֖וֹן מִיָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand? How then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria spoke with pride and challenge.
He asked about the gods of all the nations he had conquered.
He said, “No god has saved any land from my power.”
He asked, “Who among all the gods has delivered his land from my hand?”
He questioned the power of the LORD.
He said, “How can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”
passages.original: מִ֚י בְּכָל־ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽאֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־ אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִ֑י כִּי־ יַצִּ֧יל יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: But the people remained silent and did not answer a word, for Hezekiah had commanded, “Do not answer him.”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah gave a command to the people.
Hezekiah said, “Do not answer him.”
The people obeyed Hezekiah.
The people stayed silent.
The people did not say anything.
passages.original: וְהֶחֱרִ֣ישׁוּ הָעָ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ עָנ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ דָּבָ֑ר כִּי־ מִצְוַ֨ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הִ֛יא לֵאמֹ֖ר לֹ֥א תַעֲנֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Then Hilkiah’s son Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Asaph’s son Joah the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they relayed to him the words of the Rabshakeh.
passages.sermon:
Eliakim was the son of Hilkiah.
Eliakim was the palace administrator.
Shebna was the scribe.
Joah was the son of Asaph.
Joah was the recorder.
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah came to King Hezekiah.
Their clothes were torn.
They told Hezekiah the words of the Rabshakeh.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן־ חִלְקִיָּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־ עַל־ הַ֠בַּיִת וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א הַסֹּפֵ֜ר וְיוֹאָ֨ח בֶּן־ אָסָ֧ף הַמַּזְכִּ֛יר אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ דִּבְרֵ֖י רַב־ שָׁקֵֽה׃
